subject.title: Timeout compaction can report success but leave Codex channel session unrecoverable

question: When repeated timeout compactions report success but the same Codex-backed channel session keeps timing out, should OpenClaw automatically roll over/reset that session, fail with an explicit recovery action, or keep the current manual recovery boundary?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix changes persistent session-state and side-effect replay semantics across Codex app-server turns, channel delivery, and operator recovery, so code inspection alone cannot choose the product boundary.

options.title: Define replay-safe rollover
options.body: Automatically roll over or reset only sessions that have no unsafe outbound/tool side effects after the failed timeout-compaction attempts, and add tests plus live Discord/Codex proof.

options.title: Fail with explicit recovery
options.body: Do not auto-reset, but replace the success/retry loop with a precise user-facing recovery state and an in-product Doctor or reset action for the affected session.

options.title: Keep manual recovery
options.body: Accept the current manual /compact or session-store cleanup boundary and document the operational recovery instead of changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Define replay-safe rollover
recommendation.body: Automatically roll over or reset only sessions that have no unsafe outbound/tool side effects after the failed timeout-compaction attempts, and add tests plus live Discord/Codex proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Codex app-server completion-stall recovery work is the closest current-main ownership signal for session recovery after incomplete Codex turns.
